prompt.context: American Beauty Company (ABC) is a high-quality beauty products company that has performed well both in the US and globally and enjoys great brand recognition. One of their major products is hair color. ABC manufactures high-quality 'use at home' hair color products. They sell through retail and drugstores, with all manufacturing in-house. They also have an 800 number for customer support. Recently they have been experiencing declining revenues and market share. Retailers have complained about their products as the competition — Bell International — takes over. The firm has been called in to advise ABC on what to do.
prompt.question: How would you start thinking about this problem?

clarifying_info.q: What segments does the hair color market consist of?
clarifying_info.a: The major segments are Women (18–55 yrs), Men, and Teens.

clarifying_info.q: What is the current market size and growth rate by segment?
clarifying_info.a: Women: $800M, 5% growth; Men: $200M, 20% growth; Teens: $100M, 10% growth.

clarifying_info.q: What is ABC's current market share by segment?

exhibits.title: Market Size and Growth Rate by Segment
exhibits.shows: A table listing three hair color market segments with their current size (in $M) and annual growth rate.

exhibits.title: Market Size, Growth Rate, and ABC Current Market Share by Segment
exhibits.shows: The same three segments as Exhibit 1, now also showing ABC's current dollar market share percentage in each segment.

exhibits.title: Brand Awareness Survey — 18–55 yr Women
exhibits.shows: Survey results showing the percentage of respondents in each user segment who are aware of ABC vs. Bell.

data.Non_users: 40% know about ABC, 60% know about Bell

exhibits.title: Perception of Quality Survey — 18–55 yr Women
exhibits.shows: Survey results showing what percentage of respondents in each user segment believe ABC is higher quality vs. Bell is higher quality.

framework: Product: attributes, ease of use, value proposition, price, benchmark against competition and value proposition, market share and trends
Customer: target market segment(s), brand loyalty, price sensitivity, important attributes, typical customer behavior (likes/dislikes), buying habits
Distribution Channel: distribution network, shelf space and positioning relative to competitors, share of distribution network compared to competitors

questions.prompt: Part 2: ABC's biggest market segment is 18–55 year old women, but their share has been declining recently. Why might this be happening? How would you approach this issue?
questions.guidance: Suggest conducting market research to break down the issue into: brand awareness, trial %, re-trial and acceptance %, and access (distribution). Benchmark against competitor Bell to identify where ABC underperforms. Multiple root causes are possible — do not jump to one conclusion.

questions.prompt: Part 3: Using the market data (Exhibit 1 — size and growth rate only), what sales are required for ABC to have 50% of the women's market in 2 years?
questions.guidance: Candidate should note that the women's segment is maturing fast (only 5% growth). Calculate the total women's market in 2 years at 5% annual growth, then take 50% of that figure.

math.setup: Total women's market in 2 years = $800M × (1.05)^2; Target = 50% of that total.
math.answer: ABC needs $441M in sales to hold 50% of the women's market in 2 years.

questions.prompt: Part 4: What is ABC's current dollar market share? What will it be in 2 years (assuming market share percentages stay the same)?
questions.guidance: Candidate should notice ABC has very low penetration in the men's segment (only 10%), which is the fastest-growing segment at 20%/yr. This signals a major growth opportunity being missed.

math.setup: Current $ market share = sum of (segment size × ABC share %). Future $ market share = sum of (future segment size × same ABC share %). Future segment sizes use compound growth over 2 years.
math.answer: ABC's current dollar market share is $450M. In 2 years it will be approximately $506.1M, representing ~39.2% of the total market (down from a higher % today because the fast-growing men's segment dilutes ABC's overall share).

questions.prompt: Part 5: The team conducted two customer surveys (brand awareness and perception of quality) benchmarking ABC against Bell among 18–55 yr women. What do you notice and what should ABC do?
questions.guidance: Key insight: despite ABC's actual high quality and brand recognition, Bell outperforms ABC on both brand awareness and perceived quality across all segments — including Bell users, non-users, and even ABC's own users. ABC users rate Bell as higher quality (85%) more than they rate ABC as higher quality (55%). This is a brand and marketing problem, not a product quality problem. Recommendations: (1) increase advertising to improve brand awareness, (2) invest in promotions, joint marketing with retailers, and product trials to improve perception of quality.

brainstorming.prompt: Beyond the immediate brand and marketing fixes, where else should ABC look for future growth?

categories.name: Men's segment
ideas: Low current penetration (10%) in the fastest-growing segment (20%/yr)
Develop or reposition products specifically for male hair color users
Targeted advertising campaigns addressing men's grooming trends

categories.name: Teens segment
ideas: Total market size ($100M) is small but growing at 10%/yr
Opportunity to expand total market size through innovative products
Increase acceptance and usage of hair color among teens via social media and trend-focused marketing

categories.name: Distribution and retail
ideas: Address retailer complaints to improve shelf space and positioning
Joint marketing efforts with retailers to increase trial and visibility
Improve product placement relative to Bell at point of purchase

categories.name: Customer experience
ideas: Leverage 800-number customer support data to identify recurring pain points
Improve ease of use and in-box instructions to reduce trial friction
Loyalty programs to increase re-trial and retention rates

recommendation: The primary driver of declining revenues and market share is that competitor Bell has achieved superior brand awareness and perceived quality among the 18–55 yr women segment — even among ABC's own customers — despite ABC's objectively high product quality. ABC must urgently close this perception gap through advertising and aggressive promotions.
ABC should simultaneously prioritize the men's segment, where it has only 10% share in a 20%-growth market, as the primary engine for future revenue growth.
risks: The women's segment is maturing (5% growth); over-investing there may yield diminishing returns
Bell may respond to ABC's increased marketing spend with its own escalation
Men's segment may require significant product reformulation or new product lines, not just repositioning
Teens segment is small and culturally volatile; innovative products may not gain traction
next_steps: Launch a targeted advertising campaign to rebuild brand awareness in the 18–55 yr women segment
Invest in retail promotions and trial programs in partnership with key retailers to shift quality perception
Conduct deep research into the men's segment to understand unmet needs and develop a targeted go-to-market plan
Explore product innovation opportunities for the teens segment to expand total addressable market
